items.title: Decision fatigue is a routing problem — what a 3,000-year-old Chinese framework taught me about choosing
items.pt:
By 3 PM the average knowledge worker has already made ~70 decisions. By the time the important one shows up, should I take this offer, should I confront my co-founder, should I move, your brain is out of premium fuel and running on fallback heuristics.

We usually treat this as a willpower problem. It isn't. It's a routing problem: every decision gets dumped into the same queue and processed with the same tired machinery.
